key_insight: Initializing new vocabulary tokens as the mean of existing embeddings collapses them into a low‑rank, indistinct subspace; grounding token initializations in item/semantic features preserves diversity and speeds learning so tokens acquire meaningful, distinct representations.
problem_solved: How to initialize newly added vocabulary tokens (e.g., Semantic‑ID tokens for items) in pretrained LMs so they (a) avoid representational collapse from mean initialization and (b) learn useful, distinguishable embeddings with less supervised fine‑tuning.
method: Diagnose collapse: use spectral (eigenvalue) and geometric (PCA / pairwise distance) analyses to show mean initialization drives new tokens into a degenerate low‑rank subspace.

Grounded initialization: derive initial token vectors from external signals (item metadata, content embeddings, or semantically related token anchors) and align them into the LM embedding space via a lightweight mapping.
Empirical validation: compare grounded vs. mean init on convergence speed and downstream generative recommendation quality (fewer fine‑tuning steps, more discriminative token usage).
impact: Practitioners extending LMs with domain tokens can avoid slow, data‑hungry fine‑tuning and obtain more semantically meaningful tokens by grounding initial embeddings — improving convergence, interpretability, and recommendation quality with minimal extra cost.
visual_elements: Spectral plot (eigenvalue spectra) comparing mean vs. grounded initialization to show rank collapse vs. preserved spectrum.
2D PCA or t-SNE scatter of new token embeddings after initialization (and after short fine‑tuning) highlighting collapse vs. separated clusters.
Architecture diagram showing grounded initialization pipeline: item metadata → item encoder → linear alignment → token embedding in LM.
Training curves comparing convergence speed and downstream recommendation metrics for mean vs. grounded initialization.
paper_title: Grounded Token Initialization for New Vocabulary in LMs for Generative Recommendation
paper_authors: Daiwei Chen, Zhoutong Fu, Chengming Jiang, Haichao Zhang, Ran Zhou
